title: Track J global canonical dependency graph
claim_boundary: Canonical xrefs and triage labels establish static reference structure, not runtime reachability or original semantic truth. Ghidra checks are limited to high-value contract and bridge bodies.

source_artifacts.role: function classification, subsystem, cluster, evidence, decomp and vtable metadata
canonical internal call, data and vtable reference rows
exhaustive twenty-cluster partition and cluster dependency projections
xref provenance, coverage, closure and reference-type summary
cross-tool KG projection and subsystem evidence context
selected function-body evidence used by prior graph analysis and high-value checks

method.degree: Distinct internal caller and callee pairs; repeated callsites do not inflate degree.
method.components: Weak components and SCCs use only call edges whose callee is in the canonical triage universe; vtable-ref and data-ref do not join components.
method.chokepoints: Transparent proxy sqrt(distinct internal callers * distinct internal callees), requiring at least five callers and one callee; not exact betweenness.
method.root_candidates: Named singleton candidates require SDK name, gameplay category and callers. Unnamed low-out candidates require gameplay category, at least eight callers and at most four internal callees; their shared-state meaning remains a hypothesis unless body verification exists.
method.bridges: Canonical call pairs spanning gameplay and engine/runtime categories. Reference-only vtable and data edges are excluded.
method.isolated: No internal caller, internal callee or external call target. Reference-only isolated functions are counted separately.
method.evidence_order: Canonical xref and triage rows are primary; KG provides subsystem context; Ghidra bodies are targeted verification only.

subsystem_roots.role: primary gameplay state and manager root
subsystem_roots.evidence: The cluster contains 1628 functions, 1523 gameplay functions, 14435 cross-cluster call pairs and a 1334-function largest weak component. The root candidates are concentrated here and receive engine-to-gameplay bridge traffic.
App::IAppSystem::Get is a 695-caller engine interface; the cluster has 13018 cross-cluster call pairs and is the largest bridge surface outside the gameplay root.

subsystem_roots.role: editor command, message and interaction root
subsystem_roots.evidence: The three named editor surfaces are vtable dispatch/control-flow roots with no canonical internal callers and 299 total direct internal callees. cSpeciesManager::Get adds the editor state hub.
Named manager getters have low fan-out and high fan-in. Graphics has 1343 cross-cluster pairs but no gameplay category assignment, so these are engine roots rather than gameplay roots.

subsystem_roots.role: message dispatch, window and UI framework root
subsystem_roots.evidence: The cluster has 1093 functions, 66 decomp-backed rows and 4338 cross-cluster call pairs. These roots are dispatch-heavy and are downstream of many unknown-vtable implementations.
FUN_00c2e4e0 is a 198-caller inferred gameplay bridge; cAssetViewManager::Get is a named 71-caller manager root. The cluster is only 100 functions but has 830 cross-cluster pairs.
cSpaceTrading::Get is a decomp-confirmed 156-caller shared-state contract. The seven-function triage slice is too small to infer more without a broader vtable or runtime pass.

subsystem_roots.role: allocation, copy and exception substrate root
subsystem_roots.evidence: The first two are engine-implementation wrappers in unknown-fun-mass but function as global allocation/release contracts. memcpy and memset are wrapper-forest targets. This is a graph root by degree, not a gameplay semantic claim.

shared_state_roots.state_contract: unnamed global pointer or handle return

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_00f47380
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Nonzero argument forwards to FUN_009276c0; this is a high-volume release/forwarding boundary, not a semantic allocator claim.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: The target fan forest has 6527 distinct callers and 3910 leafish callers. The function is the global degree chokepoint and a major gameplay-to-engine bridge.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_00f473a0
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Forwards six arguments to FUN_009289f0; Ghidra shows repeated six-argument Editor allocation calls.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: The target fan forest has 2901 distinct callers and 1177 leafish callers. It is a shared construction/forwarding boundary used by editor and gameplay.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_00dd8640
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Complex object construction/initialization body with property queries, virtual calls, editor/engine accessors and allocation helpers.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: This is the highest-degree gameplay-logic chokepoint by the transparent proxy and a concrete semantic bridge between property data, engine services and constructed objects.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_006b55c0
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Constructs or retrieves a UI/SP::cString through FUN_00f473a0, then dispatches through an interface; used by editor message/update paths.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: A high-fan-in UI/string engine bridge with 263 callers, including the editor orchestrators. It is more actionable than the larger generic wrappers because its body establishes a typed-looking UI/SP boundary.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_00423650
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Not selected for body verification; canonical thunk edges identify the memcpy fan-forest pattern.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: High-degree copy boundary with 341 callers; structurally relevant but lower semantic value than gameplay-specific bridges.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_00b5b800
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Checks FUN_00b3d320; if nonzero, calls FUN_00a42730, otherwise returns -1.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: A narrow but heavily shared gameplay state query. It is a better first target than its fan-in alone suggests because its body exposes a gate and one engine call.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_006b5240
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Not selected for body verification; it is a repeated leaf-ish caller of the global allocation/release boundary.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: Representative leafish caller of 00f47380 with 301 callers of its own, showing wrapper-forest concentration.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_008105b0
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Not selected for body verification; it is a high-fan-in application/engine contract.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: A major app-lifecycle chokepoint with 672 callers and 1 internal callee.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_0044ae00
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Not selected for body verification; editor message/update bodies call it repeatedly.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: A gameplay-logic chokepoint inside editor command and rendering paths.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_00441440
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Not selected for body verification; it is a high fan-out app interface surface.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: Low fan-in but high fan-out interface root, useful for understanding broad app/service dispatch rather than shared state.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_00b21340
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Performs map lookup, optional callback-driven construction, linked-list traversal and callback dispatch.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: A shared state traversal/table bridge; understanding it can unlock many low-out simulator contracts that call it indirectly or share the same map/list data.

dependency_chokepoints.name: FUN_00c099e0
dependency_chokepoints.body_verification: Body initializes a simulator object, uses cSpeciesManager, cGameTimeManager, cGameInputManager and 00b3d300, then performs multiple virtual calls and transform/state updates.
dependency_chokepoints.evidence: Not a degree chokepoint by fan-in, but a high semantic leverage function: its body connects manager roots, object construction, input and state updates.

isolated_functions.definition: Zero distinct internal callers, zero distinct internal callees and zero external call targets.
isolated_functions.interpretation: Call-isolated does not mean unreachable: vtable and data references are retained but not promoted to call edges. These are parallel work packages after roots and bridges.

wrapper_forests.definition: Target fan forests detect shared-target wrapper patterns; they do not prove wrapper intent, macro origin or virtual dispatch.

thin_gameplay_external_bridges.interpretation: The compact Track I projection reports only one thin gameplay-to-external bridge; most gameplay/engine boundaries are internal wrappers and services, not direct imports.

gameplay_engine_bridges.interpretation: Bridge counts are reference-edge counts, not execution counts. The dominant pattern is gameplay code calling low-degree engine services and large allocation/release wrappers, while engine implementation code calls high-degree gameplay accessor roots.

unlock_order.objective: Freeze global and manager return contracts before reading their callers.
unlock_order.why: Highest certainty and broadest dependent set; ten named accessors have direct global returns in targeted Ghidra bodies.

unlock_order.objective: Characterize the remaining low-out contracts without assigning names from fan-in alone.
unlock_order.why: They are the next-largest gameplay dependency bottlenecks and are mostly not decomp-backed.

unlock_order.objective: Map app, graphics and simulator manager getters and their service boundaries.
unlock_order.why: Named manager roots are stable low-degree contracts and explain engine/gameplay bridge direction.

unlock_order.objective: Separate generic allocation/runtime wrappers from semantic gameplay and UI bridges.
unlock_order.why: These functions carry the highest wrapper-forest and cross-category degrees; body checks establish their one-step boundaries.

unlock_order.objective: Read dispatch/control flow after contracts are fixed; separate sequencing from leaf algorithms.
unlock_order.why: High fan-out named and vtable-backed surfaces encode subsystem boundaries and are better understood after their service roots.

unlock_order.objective: Work down coherent component boundaries, prioritizing high cross-cluster pairs and decomp-backed rows.
unlock_order.why: Cluster labels are structural and not runtime sequence; body work becomes tractable once roots and bridges are frozen.

unlock_order.objective: Resolve repeated copy, exception, allocator and leaf-like wrapper patterns only where they affect component understanding.
unlock_order.why: 390 external-only thin callers and 143 CRT-wrapper rows are broad but low-semantic-density; they should not displace root work.

unlock_order.objective: Parallelize call-isolated functions, prioritizing named, gameplay and decomp-backed rows; retain vtable/data-only membership.
unlock_order.why: These functions do not block call dependency roots, but can unlock component semantics when their vtable owners or data references are known.

limitations: The binary has no MSVC RTTI; vtable associations are candidate evidence and may merge or misattribute families.
Vtable-ref rows point to a containing vtable base, not the selected slot method; no virtual caller-to-slot edge is invented.
Canonical xrefs are static references, not execution proof; computed calls, thunks and tail calls remain bounded by exporter semantics.
The exporter does not provide a complete global data-state xref graph, so shared-state roots beyond verified body-level globals remain candidates.
Unknown-fun-mass and unknown-vtable-impl account for 49362 functions and dominate connectivity; bulk reading them before roots is inefficient.
KG subsystem nodes are manual context and do not override canonical xref counts or triage categories.
Ghidra live analysis reports 59245 functions while the canonical universe is 58757; all graph counts in this artifact use the canonical universe only.

determinism.recomputation_note: Counts are deterministic projections of the frozen v6 triage and canonical xref rows; representative edges retain actual callsites and reference types.
